source_law.title: School crossings
source_law.text: The City Traffic Engineer is authorized to mark and maintain with yellow paint or road buttons crosswalks approximately twelve feet in width at intersections in the vicinity of schools where in the opinion of the City Traffic Engineer crossing the roadway by schoolchildren is unsafe. The City Traffic Engineer, if necessary, is further authorized to mark and maintain with a distinguishing color or road buttons upon the pavement or by signs erected along the curb in a conspicuous manner, the words "School-Xing," not less than one hundred feet in advance of each crosswalk established, and it shall be unlawful for the operator of any vehicle to drive into a crosswalk where there is displayed a sign with the words "School-Xing," when there is in the crosswalk upon the side of the roadway on which said vehicle is coming any person attempting to cross the street.

physical_prerequisites: Prove the crosswalk is the marked school-area crossing addressed by the source, display a physical School-Xing sign, show a person attempting to cross within the approach-side half of the crosswalk, and measure the vehicle front footprint entering it. Record original sign/crosswalk/person pixels and source geometry; synthetic labels alone cannot establish official marking.
legal_interpretation_limit: The City Traffic Engineer authorization in text-0 is context. The text-1 vehicle prohibition applies only with the displayed School-Xing sign and a person attempting to cross on the approach side when the vehicle drives into the crosswalk. The source says person, so do not narrow this element to a schoolchild.
